svg.title: Can Babel grow today's families?
svg.desc: Rank-size plot of the 421 language lineages Glottolog recognises, against two Babel models that start them all c. 2103 BC. If every people's languages grew at one rate, the largest lineage would hold about 118 languages and there would be about 22 isolates; the world has 1,408 and 183. If peoples grew unevenly, the model's band contains the observed lineage at 328 of 421 ranks. The largest family needs a doubling every 395 years, slower than Romance's 255.
svg.text: Can lineages begun at Babel reach today's sizes?
Lineages ranked from largest to smallest
163 isolates · 258 families · median family 4 · inside the band at 328 of 421 ranks
421 lineages begun at Babel, c. 2103 BC. The largest needs a doubling every 395 years;
Romance, the fastest recorded family, doubled every 255. Bands: 10th to 90th percentile of 60 runs.
A fitted model shows the shape is reachable; it does not show this is how it happened.
After the manner of Clarence Larkin · the-way.lewy.au
